issue.title: Missing Param - SITL. Not reading position
issue.body:
Trying to read global position using SITL. This is the output I get. Lat Lon and Alt values are read as nan.
![IMG_7968](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/92040868/141012357-67a6616e-6557-4291-a2ed-5d311cc1fff6.jpg)

comments.body: What's your PX4 version and what's the MAVSDK version?

PX4: 1.12.3
I'm not sure how to check which version of MAVSDK is being run.
It looks like I'm running the latest version of mavsdk (0.48.0)
Not sure I get the problem. What is the code you run, what do you expect as a result, and what do you get instead?
Did you try running an example, e.g. https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/tree/main/examples/takeoff_and_land? Does that work?

![2021-11-15-110817_1280x1024_scrot](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/92040868/141815330-4986cf9e-3ae1-4ae1-9b20-2d127aae07c7.png)
I get this when attempting to build the example
Did you install mavsdk on your system?

I believe so. I followed the instructions found here:
https://mavsdk.mavlink.io/v0.38/en/cpp/guide/build.html

Your last screenshot shows a linking error when building the example, because the example tries to link against mavsdk. You have to solve that linking error, I cannot guess what's on your system :sweat_smile:

![2021-11-15-113103_1280x1024_scrot](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/92040868/141820139-987c130c-0092-4586-a7a3-ec5b136992ad.png)
Looks like I'm having issues building the library. Would this be a place to start?

If the cmake configure step fails ("Configuring incomplete, errors occurred"), then there is no need to try the build step :sweat_smile:.

It does not appear in your screenshot, but it seems like you are using the deprecated `-DBUILD_BACKEND=ON`, so probably you want to use a more recent version of the docs, e.g. just upstream: https://mavsdk.mavlink.io/main/en/cpp/guide/build.html.

Also to use MAVSDK-C++ (i.e. if you don't plan on using MAVSDK-Swift or MAVSDK-Java or MAVSDK-Python), no need to build mavsdk_server.

Followed the install instructions from that link. Specifically did this:

$ sudo apt-get update
$ sudo apt-get install build-essential cmake git
$ cd MAVSDK
$ git clone https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK.git
$ git submodule update --init --recursive
$ cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug -Bbuild/default -H.
$ cmake --build build/default -j8
$ cmake -Bbuild/default -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -H.
$ cmake --build build/default -j8
$ sudo cmake --build build/default --target install

Seemed to build and install properly. The linking error persists when I try to run the takeoff_and_land example. Specifically did this:
$ cd MAVSDK
$ cd examples
$ cd takeoff_and_land
$ cmake -Bbuild -H.
$ cmake --build build

Error messages come up - same as my 2nd most recent screenshot. Am I missing anything obvious?
So `$ cmake -Bbuild -H.` in the example project worked and found mavsdk on the system?

When I run `$ cmake -Bbuild -H.` here's what I get:
-- Configuring done
-- Generating done
-- Build files have been written to: /home/pi/MAVSDK/examples/takeoff_and_land/build

And do you have the symbols in the build binaries? For me:

```
% nm ./build/default/src/core/libmavsdk.so | grep subscribe_on_new_system                                                       [0]
000000000017bd0e T _ZN6mavsdk10MavsdkImpl23subscribe_on_new_systemERKSt8functionIFvvEE
00000000001771d4 T _ZN6mavsdk6Mavsdk23subscribe_on_new_systemERKSt8functionIFvvEE
```

Where would I see that? Not sure how to access build binaries. 

Really appreciate the help. I'm new to this stuff

Something like this should find it:

```
find ~/MAVSDK | grep libmavsdk.so
```
